final_disposition_2026-09-15.superseded_by: gate_d_v3_auc_reevaluation_2026-09-15 -- the Gate D heuristic used above (calibrated-threshold-sweep expectancy multiple-gain) was replaced same-day; see that section for the corrected final disposition.

gate_d_v3_auc_reevaluation_2026-09-15.why_redesigned: User-driven review identified three compounding problems with every prior Gate D design (v1 manual heuristic, v2 Kendall's-tau-on-calibrated-sweep, both same-day): (1) the sigmoid calibrator (shared/calibration/sigmoid_afml.py, calibrated_p = sigmoid(intercept + coef*logit(raw_p))) is monotonic but nonlinear -- verified empirically that XAUUSD/rangestructure_long's raw_probability spans only [0.585, 0.890], so a fixed-step threshold grid in CALIBRATED space is an uneven, arbitrary partition of the real observations, capable of stranding a handful of trades in a sparse tail bin independent of model quality (the likely cause of volatilitycarry_long's earlier spurious tail-spike pass); (2) the per-edge selected_threshold is not even the live threshold -- that is chosen later at the portfolio_allocator stage across the whole portfolio, so gating on any one sweep-selected point was testing the wrong artifact; (3) expectancy_r bundles execution/slippage/timeout noise the classifier was never trained to predict -- re-confirmed via full-text search that neither AFML nor MLAM mention 'expectancy' at all, while AFML Ch.3 pp.52-53 explicitly names the ROC curve and precision/recall/F1 as the correct diagnostic for meta-labeling quality.
gate_d_v3_auc_reevaluation_2026-09-15.new_method: shared/edges/gate_d_calibration_monotonicity.py v3: AUC-ROC between raw_probability and quote_executable_meta_label computed directly on the full per-row Step03 OOF predictions CSV (artifacts/oof/<asset>_<edge>_oof_predictions.csv) -- no binning, no threshold grid, no calibration step involved at all. Tested via one-sided Mann-Whitney U against null AUC=0.5, alpha=0.05. Because every OOF observation is used (thousands of rows) rather than ~10-20 binned points, there is no multiple-comparisons problem to correct for. A non-gating diagnostic (Kendall's tau, raw_probability vs quote_executable_r, per-row, unbinned) is also reported for economic context.
gate_d_v3_auc_reevaluation_2026-09-15.note: Notably flips trend_long and rangestructure_long to PASS -- these had the strongest Gate C exact-tick-replay evidence of the whole batch (trend_long: all 3 finalists 95% CI excludes zero; rangestructure_long: best R/occupied_day) and were incorrectly failed by both v1 and v2. volatilitycarry_long, previously rejected under v1 for a small-sample tail-spike artifact, now passes cleanly and strongly. Conversely reversal_long and timeregime_long, which had passed v1/v2 on weak evidence, do not survive the more powerful, properly-specified test.
gate_d_v3_auc_reevaluation_2026-09-15.open_followup: User flagged (2026-09-15) that the portfolio_allocator's own threshold-selection script also currently operates on the calibrated-threshold sweep -- the same dataset just shown to have calibration-plateau/uneven-binning issues. Not yet investigated; queued as the next methodology review after JPN and US500 are re-run under Gate D v3.
